title: Explore a project
example: Show what this project contains and where work stands.
outcome: A bounded view of the current Plan, sources and recorded evidence.
limitation: A read does not refresh changed files or prove that a tool ran.
description: Explore Evidence Lane, inspect the selected project and its evidence, and find the workflow that matches the request. Use for orientation or a read-only project question.

stages.description: Discover current public workflows and their registered actions without granting access.
Render the selected project registration, current Plan page, session and exact published lane references without changing work.
Search one separate lane through its current registered owner and disclose snapshot coverage.

title: Open or resume a project
example: Resume my selected project and show the current Plan.
outcome: A checked session with its exact project and saved context.
limitation: A missing native identity or mismatched saved session remains unresolved.
description: Verify the runtime and locked operating-policy package, then start or resume one explicitly selected project session. Use for project entry or client reconnection.

stages.description: Read this authenticated engine client and its explicitly configured project selections.
Verify this engine, current host observations and the locked Flash routing package.
Read the current project session, exact resume head and Plan reference.
Resume the exact project session without duplicating or silently taking over a live owner.

title: Carry out the next task
example: Continue the next eligible task and show its output and checks.
outcome: A bounded job, addressed output and recorded verification result.
limitation: A queued or failed job is not complete; changed task contracts require a Plan update.
description: Execute the next eligible project-plan task through bounded work, selected lane operations and verified completion. Use when carrying out project implementation.

stages.description: Read a bounded page of the authoritative project Plan.
Run the operation already bound to one exact Plan task through its owning Delta executor and verifier.
Read a recorded run and reconcile its completion evidence; optionally return result and verification bytes.

title: Create or update the Plan
example: Change the next task to produce a spreadsheet while preserving completed work.
outcome: One current ordered Plan with explicit scope and acceptance checks.
limitation: A steer waits for an active job to reach a safe boundary; it cannot rewrite completed history.
description: Create, inspect or safely steer the current project plan while preserving completed history and replacing only affected work. Use for planning and semantic changes.

stages.description: Read a bounded page of the authoritative project Plan.
Inspect a visible input's declared intent without changing Plan or project data.
Queue an exact visible change or stop; checkpoint an unstarted selected task, while admitted jobs keep their owning checkpoint route.
Atomically replace remaining Plan contracts after a captured steer and safe checkpoint.

title: Bring in project sources
example: Register this folder and prepare the documents and spreadsheets for my project.
outcome: An ordered source record and bounded tasks for the selected files.
limitation: Registration is not indexing. Parser coverage and current file checks are reported separately.
description: Classify, register, inspect and refresh ordered project sources with exact attribution. Use for files, selected SQLite, source identity, source graphs and authorized Git history.

stages.description: Classify ordered granted sources into retained sectors without registering or copying bytes.
Freeze and register ordered source identities and assertions in the Sources authority.
Prepare complete bounded selected-source file routes and owning Plan tasks; does not adopt a Plan or run parsers.
Run one exact prepared source group through its current Plan tasks and owning Delta verifiers, then verify coverage.

title: Exchange evidence between tasks
example: Send this result to the selected task under its stated input requirements.
outcome: An attributed packet with sender, receiver and input or return contract.
limitation: A sealed outgoing packet is not proof of receipt. Receiver acceptance remains separately owned.
description: Exchange typed requirements, evidence and results between explicitly selected project tasks while preserving sender and receiver ownership. Use for a governed task exchange.

stages.description: Version the receiver-owned typed expected-input contract.
Seal a foreign-project outbox packet, or receive a local participant exchange against its exact contract.
Receive an exact source-sealed packet as its destination participant; never mutate the source project.
Seal or reuse the content-derived typed result for the exact bound edge and pinned return contract.

title: Recall project context
example: Find the evidence behind the last completed task and its decisions.
outcome: Bounded project references with their original owners and evidence links.
limitation: Memory stores attributed locators; it does not merge source content or prove present-day freshness.
description: Ingest, query and checkpoint bounded project memory with source attribution. Use for project recall while keeping host recall, instructions, task exchanges and procedural lessons separate.

stages.description: Search a bounded project-local locator slice without loading source payloads.
Pin a bounded Memory slice to current Plan and attributed visible lineage.
Read a checkpoint slice with explicit attribution and current compatibility.

title: Inspect project lessons
example: Show lessons from verified work that are relevant to this task.
outcome: Project-local lessons with verification provenance and retained revocation history.
limitation: Host recall is separate. Referencing host memory does not create a verified lesson.
description: Inspect and revoke project-isolated procedural lessons recorded after verified work, or record an explicit host-memory provenance reference without creating a lesson. Use for lesson retrieval, correction or provenance.

stages.description: Retrieve a bounded project-local slice of verified execution observations.
Revoke the exact current Learning observation and suppress automatic reactivation.
Retrieve a bounded project-local slice of verified execution observations.

title: Understand applicable instructions
example: Show the instruction chain for this project folder.
outcome: File provenance, override order and separately identified recall sources.
limitation: Observed files do not prove what a particular Codex task actually loaded.
description: Inspect the selected instruction chain and explicitly selected host recall without merging either into project evidence. Use for instruction provenance and recall boundaries.

stages.description: Inspect scoped instruction and separate workspace/host recall file hashes; never import or modify their contents.

title: Shape the project workflow
example: Use these selected sources to propose a workflow for a research report.
outcome: A proposal tying the requested outcome to source types and relevant checks.
limitation: A proposal neither changes the Plan nor grants permission to execute.
description: Derive or change the project workflow from explicitly selected sources and the requested outcome. Use during initial project classification or an explicit workflow change.

stages.description: Propose Git or content-only project workflows from a complete registered batch and current lane contracts without changing Plan or sources.
Read a bounded page of the authoritative project Plan.

title: Clarify the kind of work
example: Classify this document review and explain its relevant checks.
outcome: A classification with suitable source types, work units and validation gates.
limitation: Inferred classifications are labeled; classification alone cannot start work.
description: Classify the requested work, relevant source lanes, action classes and required gates. Use for known work patterns or an explicit custom classification; classification does not authorize execution.

stages.description: Classify ordered work policies, owning lanes and action classes without creating a sector or authorizing work.
Inspect ordered compatible routes for an authorized operation without invoking or installing tools.

title: Fit evidence into context
example: Select the most relevant evidence within a 2000-token estimate.
outcome: A deterministic selection of attributed references within explicit budgets.
limitation: Token counts are estimates. Selection does not fetch or reverify raw source content.
description: Select attributed project evidence within explicit item and estimated-token budgets. Use to fit the relevant evidence into context without merging its owning stores.

stages.description: Select deterministic metadata slices using explicit estimated-token and item budgets; verify content through its owning authority.
Fetch bounded immutable source bytes through the owning lane using an exact snapshot and path.

title: Refresh changed evidence
example: Refresh the selected spreadsheet after these source changes.
outcome: Updated selected source snapshots and requested derived views.
limitation: Refresh does not automatically parse every source or render every possible view.
description: Refresh selected sources, lane views and changed authority references after a steer or verified work. Use for explicit evidence refresh and stale view repair.

stages.description: Prepare changed, new and deleted selected sources as exact owning parser and retirement Plan tasks; preserve unselected scopes and history.
Atomically replace remaining Plan contracts after a captured steer and safe checkpoint.
Run one exact prepared source group through its current Plan tasks and owning Delta verifiers, then verify coverage.
Export only selected lane artifacts from an exact verified source preview.

title: Inspect connections
example: Show which connectors this project can use and when their grants expire.
outcome: Current connector registrations, scope, versions and configured backend references.
limitation: Registration is separate from measured execution readiness.
description: Inspect connector grants and their runtime readiness within an Evidence Lane project. Use for connector orientation; configuration and revocation have separate workflows.

stages.description: Inspect a bounded project registration page and current scope choices without activating a backend.
Inspect ordered compatible routes for an authorized operation without invoking or installing tools.

title: Configure a connection
example: Configure the selected registered adapter for this exact project resource.
outcome: A versioned connector definition with bounded actions, targets and expiry.
limitation: Saving configuration cannot install an arbitrary adapter or grant project administration.
description: Configure an Evidence Lane project connector and its bounded grant. Use to add or change connector access within that project.

stages.description: Inspect a bounded project registration page and current scope choices without activating a backend.
Add or configure one versioned project extension grant without executing its backend.
Inspect a bounded project registration page and current scope choices without activating a backend.

title: Withdraw a connection
example: Revoke this project connector and retain its history.
outcome: The exact grant is revoked and its historical receipts remain inspectable.
limitation: Revocation does not uninstall the provider, remove project data or revoke unrelated grants.
description: Revoke one Evidence Lane project connector grant while preserving its recorded history. Use for explicit withdrawal of connector access.

stages.description: Inspect a bounded project registration page and current scope choices without activating a backend.
Revoke the exact reviewed project extension version while preserving its history.
Inspect a bounded project registration page and current scope choices without activating a backend.

title: Inspect and select tools
example: Check which tools can perform this task on my current machine.
outcome: A primary route and declared alternatives with measured readiness requirements.
limitation: An unavailable tool stays unavailable. Uncertain effects are not silently retried with another tool.
description: Inspect and select lane operation tools, ordered fallbacks and measured compute readiness. Use for toolchain resolution or project accelerator configuration.

stages.description: Read shared tool declarations and executable operation routes; installation and execution remain separately qualified.
Inspect ordered compatible routes for an authorized operation without invoking or installing tools.
Read measured tools/providers, worker state and selected-project job health.

title: Choose project storage
example: Register this source folder with a separate durable project-state folder.
outcome: Distinct source and state roots with separately owned project records.
limitation: Persistent local Windows only. Registering roots does not migrate existing data or prove that source indexing has run.
description: Register or inspect persistent local project state and its separate lane databases. Use for local project root selection.

stages.description: Register an existing project root or create one direct flat PV root, intake its selected source lane first, then initialize retained authorities without unrelated sectors.
Read distinct source, state, engine and plugin roots and the exact published lane references.

title: Explore linked evidence
example: Show how this project’s sources and tasks relate to its recorded results.
outcome: A bounded attributed map with source, task and selected project references.
limitation: Links do not grant access; a recorded relationship does not imply current target access.
description: Inspect and maintain one project's explicitly linked evidence and project references with attributed read-only queries. Use for integrity checks and selected project links.

stages.description: Verify coherent project evidence head coordinator, initialized lane heads and bounded registered-file identities without refresh.
Read or literally filter bounded project evidence head coordinator, lane, Plan, Source and project-link nodes; follow category cursors.
Read this project's attributed links without opening or authorizing their targets.

title: Link separate projects
example: Connect the selected projects through a separate evidence network.
outcome: A hash-reference network while each project keeps its own databases and files.
limitation: The coordinator is separate from members. Snapshots are not simultaneous freshness guarantees.
description: Register and link hash-only project summaries in a separate cross-project network without merging project data. Use only for an explicitly selected network.

stages.description: Create an explicitly selected federation in a separate coordinator project.
Capture verified member lane hashes, reuse unchanged content and preserve historical heads.
Append a hash-only cross-project edge under its exact active grant and current member read access.
Verify bounded federation identities, historical heads and explicit grant links.

title: Transfer work to another client
example: Transfer this project at a safe boundary to the selected client.
outcome: An exact offer, destination acceptance and attributed continuation context.
limitation: A title or client label cannot prove native task identity. Missing required attestation stops transfer.
description: Transfer current project work between explicitly selected clients with exact ownership checks and attributed continuation context. Use for a requested task handoff.

stages.description: Read attributed Plan, task exchange authority, Memory and lineage locators for an accepted project continuation.
Offer exact project-participant continuity to another registered client at a safe work boundary.
Accept a destination-pinned project continuation and put the source client in read-only closeout.
Resume the exact project session without duplicating or silently taking over a live owner.

title: Back up or recover a project
example: Create and verify a coherent project backup before recovery.
outcome: A checked backup of separate records or a fresh recovery destination.
limitation: Offline recovery requires a stopped engine. It preserves the original root and never claims failed work succeeded.
description: Back up separate project lanes coherently, restore selected Git history to a fresh folder, or recover after client loss. Use for explicit recovery; accepted-PV rollback is removed.

stages.description: Inspect registered files, unregistered leftovers and database recovery status without repair.
Create and verify a consistent project database and registered-file backup.
Hash-check an exact project backup without restoring it.

title: Close a project session
example: Close this session after the current work reaches a safe boundary.
outcome: A recorded session closure and detached capture.
limitation: Closing a session does not delete data, stop the shared engine or complete a native Goal.
description: Close the selected Evidence Lane project session at a safe work boundary and detach its Flash and capture. Use when explicitly ending that session.

stages.description: Read the current project session, exact resume head and Plan reference.
Close the exact current session at a safe boundary and detach its capture binding.
Read the current project session, exact resume head and Plan reference.

title: Coordinate end-to-end work
example: Take this project from selected sources through a Plan to a verified result.
outcome: The owning workflows coordinate entry, planning, work, evidence and closure.
limitation: Each step retains its own checks and permissions. A lifecycle request cannot bypass a failed gate.
description: Coordinate project entry, planning, bounded implementation, evidence refresh and session closure across the owning first-class workflows. Use for the complete Evidence Lane project lifecycle.

stages.description: Boot one project session with verified Flash and attributed capture.
Read a bounded page of the authoritative project Plan.
Run the operation already bound to one exact Plan task through its owning Delta executor and verifier.
Read a recorded run and reconcile its completion evidence; optionally return result and verification bytes.
Close the exact current session at a safe boundary and detach its capture binding.
